markdown:
## Bottom line
**Suggests Benign (65%)** · Unreliable input · Careful review
Benign and InSitu are not separated at 90%; the input is flagged. [F1]

## Confidence
| Signal | Value | Reading |
|---|---|---|
| Top probabilities | Benign 65%, InSitu 34%, Invasive 0% | Benign leads |
| Conformal set | Benign, InSitu (90%) | Cannot separate the two |
| Reliability / OOD | 0.77 / OOD 1.0 [F6] | Input flagged |
| Second-model (MUSK) agreement | No | Top classes differ |
| Similar cases | 2 of 5 Benign [F5] | Neighbors lean InSitu |

## Tissue evidence
- **Dense lymphocytic infiltrate** (regions 0, 4, 8) · context · Scored above typical; descriptive only · Weak
- **Tumor infiltrating stroma** (region 1) · ↓ invasive · Scored below typical; little invasive signal · Validated
- **Atypical cells confined within ducts** (regions 5, 6, 9) · ↓ invasive · Scored above typical; points away from invasion · Weak
- **Marked nuclear pleomorphism** (region 11) · ↓ invasive · Scored low; slightly lowers invasive association · Validated

## Trust check
- **Heatmap**: Removing the top 3 regions drops the invasive logit 0.54 more than random (CI 0.47–0.60); faithful to the classifier.
- **Concepts**: Deletion effect 0.002 vs random (CI −0.005 to 0.007) includes 0; not shown to reflect the classifier. Mitoses, necrosis and normal lobules are Unreliable (0/20, 3/20, 0/20).

## Could be wrong if
- Simulated JPEG degradation and flagged input may distort probabilities; reliability ranks errors modestly (AUROC 0.69).
- The second model disagrees and only 2 of 5 neighbors are Benign; InSitu may be correct.

## Check on the slide
1. **Regions 5, 6, 9**: confirm atypical cells are confined to ducts; separate in situ from benign.
2. **Region 1**: highest regional invasive probability (50%); look for stromal invasion.
3. **Regions 0, 4, 8**: verify the lymphocytic infiltrate; its spot check was only 8/20.
